claims.text: DFT with phonon-dispersion calculations can accurately identify high-entropy alloys having low phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed approach applies to high-entropy alloys in an initial, unprocessed state.
Phonon dispersion and lattice dynamics are the structural mediators relevant to predicting phonon thermal conductivity.
Ab initio phonon-dispersion and lattice-thermal-conductivity calculations provide the mechanism by which the approach identifies low-conductivity alloys.
The proposed method will predict low phonon thermal conductivity more accurately than current methods.
Use of the proposed predictive method could produce a 10–20% reduction in thermal conductivity.
The approach is applicable only to high-entropy alloys and thermal-insulation applications.
Computational complexity may limit the approach's applicability.
The approach requires high-quality input data.
Alloy microstructure and defects may affect phonon thermal conductivity and the method's improvement.
Failure to improve prediction accuracy by more than 5% relative to current methods would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention is a computational prediction method, but the predicted outcome includes a 10–20% physical reduction in thermal conductivity. A predictive method can identify lower-conductivity materials or reduce prediction error, but it does not itself reduce a material's conductivity.
